title: Marked-Code Counting Run
statement: Fix natural numbers $K_0,B,P$, an oracle $\mathrm{orc}:\{0,1,2,3\}\times\{0,1\}^*\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, and a finite bit string $x$. For a Boolean $\varphi$, a natural number $j$, a register state $S$, and a memory function $M:\mathbb Z\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, suppose that $S.K-S.U=j$ (with truncated natural-number subtraction), $S.U\le S.K$, $S.T=S.T_2=S.Z=0$, and $S.c+(S.K-S.U)\le S.K$. Suppose also that every register of $S$ is at most $B$, that $S.B_s+S.K\le B$, $S.B_s+S.K\le P$, and $S.K+1\le B$. Then the machine has a finite run from the count-search configuration with registers $S$, memory $M$, and memory-head position $0$ to the branch for $\varphi$, with $U=S.K$ and $c$ equal to its initial value plus the number of integers $v$ in $[S.U,S.K)$ for which $M(S.B_s+v)=\mathrm{true}$. Every other register retains its initial value, and the safety guard holds at every configuration before the endpoint.
hypotheses_covered: $\mathrm{orc}$ is an oracle from four query types and finite bit strings to Boolean answers

Fix a machine parameter $K_0$, an oracle, an input, and natural-number bounds $B$ and
$P$. Let $varphi$ be a Boolean, $j$ a natural number, $S$ a register state, and $M$ a
memory function. Suppose $S.K-S.U=j$, $S.U\leq S.K$, $S.T=S.T2=S.Z=0$, and
$S.c+(S.K-S.U)\leq S.K$, where subtraction is truncated subtraction on natural numbers.
Assume also that every register in $S$ is at most $B$, that $S.Bs+S.K\leq B$ and
$S.Bs+S.K\leq P$, and that $S.K+1\leq B$. Starting from the count-search state with
registers $S$ and memory $M$ at head position $0$, the machine reaches the branch
determined by $varphi$, with register $U$ equal to $S.K$ and register $c$ increased by
the number of indices $v$ in the half-open interval $[S.U,S.K)$ for which the memory bit
at position $S.Bs+v$ is true; all other registers equal their values in $S$, and the run
satisfies the specified safety guard at every preceding step.
